summary.headline: Orders and revenue beat target this week despite WoW declines, but YTD revenue remains behind target and the 14-Day Return Rate shows an anomalous jump.

points.what: Orders came in at 989, 110.6% of target, down 6.7% WoW.
points.so_what: The week stayed ahead of target even as volume pulled back, keeping the quarter's order performance on the ahead side of target.

points.what: Revenue was 74081, 109.5% of target, down 5.0% WoW.
points.so_what: Revenue also cleared target despite the pullback, contributing to the quarter's 100.7% QTD attainment.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 25 May rose to 11.7%, up 2.7pp WoW, flagged as an anomaly.
points.so_what: The anomaly flag means this increase is unusual, not a typical week-to-week move, and marks a fresh risk to order quality.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment stands at 96.7%, behind target.
points.so_what: Even with two ahead-of-target weekly results, the year overall remains behind, and the recent pace falls short of what full-year attainment requires.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.4%, up 0.8pp WoW and up 1.7pp YoY, both rated bad.
points.so_what: A rise in both WoW and YoY terms means cancellations continue moving in the wrong direction, working against the revenue captured this week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 25 May rose to 11.7%, up 2.7pp WoW and up 1.9pp YoY, flagged as an anomaly.
points.so_what: The anomaly flag means this jump is unusual rather than typical week-to-week movement, marking a risk to order quality that stands out from recent weeks.

points.what: New signups fell to 223, down 20.6% WoW and down 11.2% YoY, both rated bad.
points.so_what: A notable drop in new signups while orders kept growing YoY is a risk to sustaining that order growth if the gap continues.

points.what: Orders were 110.6% of target and revenue was 109.5% of target this week, both rated ahead.
points.so_what: Both weekly KPIs cleared target despite WoW declines, keeping the week in ahead-of-target territory alongside the quarter's ahead position.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 100.7%, ahead of target, with 2 weeks left in the quarter and 136509 still needed to reach the full-quarter target.
points.so_what: The quarter is currently ahead of target but not yet secured, with the full remaining amount still to be delivered in the last two weeks.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 96.7%, behind target, and requires a weekly run rate of 83488 against a recent 8-week run rate of 70092.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year target is out of reach unless the weekly pace rises well above the recent run rate.

points.what: EMEA orders fell to 170, down 22.0% WoW, the largest contributor to the week's order decline at 67.6% of the change.
points.so_what: EMEA alone accounted for most of the week's order pullback, making it the region driving the overall decline.

points.what: Search orders fell to 711, down 6.7% WoW, contributing 71.8% of the week's order decline.
points.so_what: Since Search is the largest traffic source, its pullback was the main reason total orders fell WoW, rather than weakness spread evenly across channels.

points.what: Facebook orders rose to 65, up 18.2% WoW, adding orders while other channels fell.
points.so_what: Facebook was the only channel growing WoW, but its gain was not enough to offset the declines in Search and other channels.

points.what: AOV rose to 88.51, up 2.7% WoW and 3.2% YoY, both rated good.
points.so_what: Since orders fell 6.7% WoW while revenue fell only 5.0% WoW, the smaller revenue decline came from the higher AOV rather than from order volume.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.4%, up 0.8pp WoW and up 1.7pp YoY, both rated bad.
points.so_what: At $875 of revenue per cancellation point, the higher rate represents revenue lost against this week's target.

points.what: New signups fell to 223, down 20.6% WoW and down 11.2% YoY, both rated bad, even as orders grew 88.4% YoY.
points.so_what: New signup growth continues to lag order growth, a risk to sustaining that order growth if the gap persists.

anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
